Swami Ramanujar continued his stay in Sri Rangam. He continued to attempt to gain access to the Ranganatha Perumal temple keys to reform the way the temple was being administered. The temple keys were being held by a person named Periya Kovil Nambi. Periya Kovil Nambi was a man with a harsh temperament and was very stubborn. However much Swami Ramanujar tried to get the temple keys, Periya Kovil Nambi would avoid Swami Ramanujar. Before Periya Kovil Nambi became a respected person in charge of temple administration, he was a gambler. Periya Kovil Nambi's mother came to Swami Ramanujar for help to reform her son's behavior. Swami Ramanujar went to the gambling house to observe Periya Kovil Nambi. After observing Periya Kovil Nambi's behavior, Swami Ramanujar sends Kurathalwan to retrieve Periya Kovil Nambi from the gambling house to initiate reform.

Kurathalwan taught Periya Kovil Nambi the shastras and various vyakyanams, transforming the gambler into a respectable man who earned the right to control the temple administration. Over time, Periya Kovil Nambi began to develop a superiority complex, as he had the sole right to control the temple and oversee its operation. In his opinion, he was above everyone except Ranganatha Perumal. Swami Ramanujar noticed that there were errors in the way he was conducting the temple rituals and hence deemed it necessary to gain access to the temple keys to change the way the temple was being administered. 

One day, Periya Kovil Nambi was conducting a homam for which he required a learned acharya to be present for a position known as Ekaham. At the time, it was customary to visit Swami Ramanujar to bless such occasions. Thus, Periya Kovil Nambi came to Swami Ramanujar to grace the event. Swami Ramanujar said he would send his guru, Kurathalwan, to grace the occasion. Periya Kovil Nambi was delighted to hear that his guru would be gracing the event. After the conduction of the homam, it was customary to give daanam to the person taking the position of Ekaham. The custom of providing daanam was to continue giving until the person receiving the daanam said they were satisfied. Thus, Periya Kovil Nambi began to offer daanam to his guru, and after the daanam, he would ask if his guru was satisfied. Kurathalwan would reply that he was not happy. Soon, it came to a point where Periya Kovil Nambi asked his guru what it would take to earn his satisfaction. When this question was asked, Kurathalwan asked for the keys to the temple. Periya Kovil Nambi handed over the keys of the temple to Kurathalwan, who, in turn, handed them to Swami Ramanujar. 

Swami Ramanujar immediately took charge of all the temple activities. He established all the rituals that are practiced at the temple to date. When Periya Kovil Nambi noticed the changes, he realized that he was at fault. Swami Ramanujar then handed the keys back to Periya Kovil Nambi. Periya Kovil Nambi promises to uphold the traditions established by Swami Ramanujar.
